title: Reborn with Purpose
next_chapter_hook: Deep within the Imperial City, the phoenix carriage swayed gently. The summons from Princess Taiping had arrived at the courier station. Chen Ji gazed at the token adorned with golden silk phoenix patterns, his fingertips growing cold—this gamble involved his very life and death.

text.content: Chen Nian's words were like a fine needle, piercing deep into Chen Ji's heart. 'Trust no one, not even yourself.' He chewed on these words, feeling as if all his blood was flowing backward. Yet he could not stop. The chess game of the realm had reached its middle phase—if he retreated, those behind him would have no chance of survival.

He tucked the blanket tighter around his sister and turned away, his expression already restored to its usual calm. Three days later, at the East Huamen Gate of the Imperial City, a small blue-cloth sedan chair waited quietly. As the curtain lifted, Chen Ji changed into a dark cyan robe, his face gaunt, his brow serene with a worldly detachment he hadn't possessed before. He looked at himself in the mirror—the person reflected was terrifyingly unfamiliar.

Master Longyuan. He silently recited this new name, as if reciting a death warrant. Mo Xiansheng had said that the aura of the Tianji Record Fragment would be suppressed by the dynasty's dragon qi. As long as he didn't actively expose himself, no one would see through his background in the short term. But how long was 'short term'? He didn't know. Yet the Crown Prince had no time left.

In the side hall of the Eastern Palace, candlelight flickered. Crown Prince Li Chengyan sat枯坐 at his desk, before him piled high with memorials—all impeachment documents against him. The Xuanwu Sect-backed Second Prince pressed closer with each passing day, officials from the Ministry of Revenue and War were being purged one after another, and his position as Crown Prince was already tottering.

dialogue.content: Your Highness, Longyuan requests an audience.

text.content: Silence hung in the hall for a moment before the eunuch's shrill voice rang out: 'Admit him.' Chen Ji strode in, eyes forward, offering the Crown Prince a half-bow. His peripheral vision swept across the cold ginseng soup on the prince's desk, and he had already calculated the situation—this prince hadn't eaten a proper meal in three days.

The Crown Prince studied him, his gaze containing both scrutiny and the desperate urgency of a drowning man grasping at driftwood. 'Are you the prodigy my father spoke of?' Chen Ji smiled faintly—a smile thin as mountain mist, yet carrying an undeniable certainty that could not be ignored.

dialogue.content: A prodigy is too grand a title. If Your Highness trusts me, I have three strategies that can stabilize your kingdom.

text.content: These words fell, and even the breathing in the hall became audible. The Crown Prince leapt to his feet, his wide sleeves knocking over the inkstone, black ink spilling across the floor unheeded. 'Please, speak, Master!' Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back, his voice neither loud nor soft, yet each word crystal clear: 'First—abandon the pieces.'

Abandon the pieces? The Crown Prince froze. Chen Ji continued: 'Among Your Highness's thirty-seven Eastern Palace officials, at least ten are spies for the Second Prince. Rather than letting them continue to hollow out Your Highness's foundations, it would be better to actively 'demote' a few of them out of the capital.' He paused. 'When the Second Prince believes he has succeeded, he will lower his guard.'

The Crown Prince's eyes flickered with momentary brightness, then wavered. 'But those were all officials my father assigned years ago...' Chen Ji smiled lightly: 'Your Highness, in royalty there are no fathers and sons—only ruler and subject. Did His Majesty assign them because he trusted them, or to spy on Your Highness? Does Your Highness truly not know?'

These were heavy words. The Crown Prince's face changed dramatically. But Chen Ji gave him no chance to rebut, shifting topics: 'Second—form alliances. Han Lie controls the Xuanwu Sect, yet he and the Second Prince are in name only. If Your Highness can find fractures within the Xuanwu Sect, you can turn Han Lie's blade against the Second Prince.'

Form alliances... The Crown Prince murmured, as if digesting the meaning of these words. Chen Ji's fingers moved subtly within his sleeve, calculating the timing—he wagered the Crown Prince's mind was still clear at this moment. As expected, the Crown Prince looked up sharply: 'And the third?'

dialogue.content: Third—seize fate. The Ancient Forbidden Land is about to open. If Your Highness can grasp even a fraction of the opportunities within, it would be a struggle against heaven itself. Then, Your Majesty will see clearly who truly possesses the mettle to bear great responsibility.

text.content: The Crown Prince fell silent for a long while, then suddenly burst into laughter—laughter tinged with tears. 'Excellent! Excellent, Master Longyuan!' He bowed deeply. 'If Master can help me survive this crisis, I shall share the world with Master!' Chen Ji returned the bow, neither servile nor arrogant: 'Your Highness flatters. Longyuan merely seeks a place to rest.'

The sovereign and minister were conversing pleasantly when sudden commotion arose outside the hall. A panicked eunuch rushed in and knelt: 'Your Highness, Han Lie of the Xuanwu Sect requests an urgent audience!' The Crown Prince's expression shifted slightly as he looked toward Chen Ji. Chen Ji lowered his eyes, a barely perceptible smile curving his lips—here he comes.

choice.prompt: Han Lie's arrival is suspicious, clearly targeting the Crown Prince. How should Master Longyuan respond?

choices.text: Retreat gracefully behind the screen and observe calmly
choices.description: Let the Crown Prince handle it first while secretly observing Han Lie's intentions and cards
choices.risk_hint: Risk missing the opportunity to publicly humiliate

text.content: Chen Ji gave the Crown Prince a slight nod and silently retreated behind the screen on the side of the hall. His breathing slowed to barely perceptible, yet his heartbeat grew increasingly steady. Han Lie possessed overwhelming Combat Power but was weak in strategy—if he dared to storm the Eastern Palace at this time, he was either relying on strong backing, or... being used as someone's pawn.

choices.text: Confront him directly as a strategist
choices.description: Reveal identity and confront Han Lie head-on, using words to probe his bottom line.
choices.risk_hint: Han Lie's Combat Power is staggering; direct conflict carries risk

text.content: Chen Ji did not retreat. The Crown Prince started to speak, but saw this newly recruited strategist step forward slowly, cupping his hands: "Your Highness, since Long Yuan has entered the Eastern Palace, there is no reason for retreat." His voice was not loud, yet carried an undeniable certainty. The Crown Prince froze, momentarily speechless.

choices.text: Take the initiative to strike first and expose his intentions
choices.description: Don't wait for Han Lie to speak—reveal his purpose first and catch him off guard.
choices.risk_hint: Will raise suspicions about his intelligence sources

text.content: Han Lie strode into the hall like a falling meteor, utterly disregarding the Crown Prince. Just as he was about to speak, Chen Ji smiled first: "Lord Han, visiting so late at night—I presume you're here about this morning's memorial impeaching the Eastern Palace? I wonder what Second Prince promised you, Your Excellency—perhaps the position of next sect master of Xuanwu Sect, or a promise of half the empire?"

The great hall doors burst open as a burly figure strode in. Han Lie wore dark iron light armor, radiating killing intent as if just returned from battle. His gaze swept across the hall before landing on Chen Ji, his brow furrowing slightly: "Who are you? Since when did the Eastern Palace have such a figure?" His tone was arrogant, clearly dismissing Chen Ji.

Chen Ji returned the salute unhurriedly, his voice mild as if making casual conversation: "I am Long Yuan, and I have long admired Lord Han's prestige." He raised his eyes—those calm, unrippled eyes caused Han Lie to inexplicably feel a flicker of unease. "Your Excellency visits so late at night; surely you have important business? Please speak frankly, so I may assist His Highness."

Han Lie coldly snorted. He drew a memorial from his breast and hurled it onto the table: "Your Highness, this general comes tonight bearing the Emperor's secret decree—to thoroughly investigate the Eastern Palace for collusion with the Demonic Path!" The moment these words fell, the hall's temperature seemed to plummet ten degrees. The Crown Prince's face turned ashen, instinctively stepping back. Chen Ji remained utterly unmoved, even lowering his head to glance at the memorial.

dialogue.content: Collusion with the Demonic Path? What a grand accusation, Lord Han. I merely wonder—was this secret decree personally written by His Majesty, or did someone forge it?

text.content: This question struck at the heart. Han Lie's expression darkened, coldly laughing: "A strategist of unknown origin dares question an imperial decree?" His Yuanli surged, warping the air around him. "Your Highness, this general suspects this person has connections to the Demonic Path. I request Your Highness permit a thorough examination on the spot!" The Crown Prince opened his mouth but found no words—he might be the nation's heir, but he truly could not afford to offend Han Lie.

choice.prompt: Han Lie wants to examine you on the spot. How will you respond?

choices.text: Retreat to advance—let the Crown Prince decide
choices.description: Kick the ball to the Crown Prince, forcing him to step out and protect you, thereby tightening the alliance of interests.
choices.visible_reward: The Crown Prince will owe you a favor
choices.risk_hint: The Crown Prince may not withstand the pressure

text.content: Chen Ji did not defend himself. He only turned to the Crown Prince and performed a deep bow: "Your Highness, Long Yuan is new here, with neither fame nor standing. If Your Highness does not trust Long Yuan, then permit Lord Han to examine me as he wishes." He spoke calmly, but the Crown Prince heard the subtext—if even he, as ruler, dare not protect his own people, who would ever serve him again?

choices.text: Counterattack on the spot, exposing Han Lie's damaging evidence
choices.description: Present pre-prepared evidence to publicly humiliate Han Lie
choices.risk_hint: The source of evidence may arouse suspicion

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly smiled, his laughter clear and bright: "Since Commander Han wants to investigate, I dare to ask a question—did the Commander's memorial mention evidence of the Eastern Palace colluding with the Demonic Path?" He took out a token from his sleeve. "Coincidentally, I also have something here: an account of Commander Han's subordinate Li Hu meeting in secret with the Second Prince three days ago. Would the Commander like to hear it?"

The atmosphere in the hall froze like ice. Han Lie's killing intent stalled, a flash of astonishment flickering in his eyes. He stared fixedly at Chen Ji, as if trying to see through this scholar-advisor's weak exterior to discover what lay hidden beneath. "You..." His voice tightened slightly, "Are you threatening me?" Chen Ji shook his head, his tone mild to the point of being almost compassionate: "I am merely reminding the Commander that His Majesty's wisdom shines bright. Some things can be hidden for a time, but not for a lifetime."

Han Lie's face turned ashen. He suddenly burst into laughter, but within the laughter was a cold, sinister edge: "Good! Well said, Master Longyuan!" He swept his sleeves and turned away. At the hall's entrance, he suddenly looked back. "This debt, this general will remember. When we meet on the battlefield someday, I hope the Master will still remember today's words!" With that, he strode away, leaving chaos in his wake.

The Crown Prince let out a long breath, his entire body seemingly drained as he slumped into his chair. His gaze toward Chen Ji had changed, carrying three parts reverence, three parts gratitude, and four parts indefinable wariness. "Master... how did the Master come to know of those matters?" Chen Ji lowered his eyes, his expression tranquil: "Your Highness, there are some things that it is better not to know too much about."

The Crown Prince was stunned for a moment, then gave a bitter laugh: "The Master speaks truly. Only today do I realize that this court is a hundred times more dangerous than I imagined." He stood up and formally clasped his hands in salute to Chen Ji. "From now on, the entire Eastern Palace shall be at the Master's disposal. Whatever the Master requires, I will not refuse." Chen Ji returned the salute, but in his heart he was calculating—trust from the Crown Prince came too quickly. How much was genuine, how much was exploitation? He would need to observe slowly.

That night, the Eastern Palace blazed with lights. Chen Ji drafted detailed strategies for the Abandonment, Alliance, and Fate-Seizing plans through the night, each point striking directly at the要害. The more the Crown Prince read, the more alarmed he became—this Master Longyuan's understanding of court politics, his insight into human hearts, was like an old fox that had been lurking for decades. Yet the man was clearly only thirty or so years old.

The next day, the streets and alleys of the imperial capital were abuzz with two topics: First, that Xuanwu Sect's Han Lie had been humiliated at the Eastern Palace last night, reportedly being publicly disgraced by an unknown strategist; second, that this mysteriously enigmatic "Master Longyuan" had overnight become the Crown Prince's honored guest.

Word reached a secluded palace deep within the imperial compound. Princess Taiping Li Zhaoning set down her teacup, a knowing smile playing at the corners of her lips. "Master Longyuan?" she murmured, tasting the name. "How interesting." She beckoned to her attendant female official. "Go to the驿馆 and deliver a message: the Princess wishes to host a banquet in the Imperial Gardens tomorrow and requests Master Longyuan's gracious presence."

When Chen Ji received the invitation, he was conversing in the back courtyard of the驿馆 with Master Mo's remnant soul. After hearing his plan, Master Mo fell silent for a long while before speaking: "Are you certain you want to take root in this imperial dynasty? The dragon's energy here may conceal the Tianji Record, but it is also the most dangerous place in the world. Once exposed, it will be utter destruction."

dialogue.content: I have no retreat. Chen Nian is in the hands of the Eye of Heavenly Dao, and the opportunity in the Forbidden Grounds cannot wait. The imperial dynasty is the greatest power I can currently leverage.

text.content: Master Mo's remnant soul sighed, dissolving into blue mist that scattered in the air. Chen Ji lowered his head to gaze at the phoenix-patterned token in his hand, his fingertips tracing the patterns. Princess Taiping—the most honored woman in the empire, reportedly even the Emperor gave way to her. Her summons—fortune or misfortune?

He suddenly remembered his sister's warning. "Trust no one, including yourself." Chen Ji gripped the token tightly, a self-deprecating curve forming at the corner of his lips. Indeed, if he couldn't even trust himself, how could he fathom that princess deep within the palace? But some games, once entered, cannot be retreated from. He took a deep breath and tucked the token into his sleeve.

choice.prompt: Princess Taiping has summoned you. How should you prepare for this meeting?

choices.text: Inquire about the Princess's preferences, prepare to cater to her tastes
choices.description: Know yourself and know your enemy—first gauge the Princess's temperament and preferences before responding
choices.risk_hint: May expose that you are investigating the Princess

text.content: Chen Ji mobilized his connections through the night, gathering information about Princess Taiping's preferences from various channels. The reports arrived quickly at his desk: this woman possessed both talent and beauty, particularly fond of the game of Go, and even more so of those who could watch in silence without speaking; her temperament was proud, and she despised flatterers; it was said she remained unmarried to this day, and no one in the imperial capital dared to mention this matter.

choices.text: Proactively show weakness, retreat to advance
choices.description: Be neither servile nor arrogant, making the princess find you interesting but not a threat.
choices.visible_cost: May be seen as an ordinary person

text.content: After pondering for a moment, Chen Ji decided to respond with constancy to all changes. He had always excelled at playing the fool before striking. When dealing with such a high-and-mighty noble, the best approach was to let her believe she controlled everything. The true chess master always hides behind the chessboard.

choices.description: Prepare something sufficient to spark the princess's interest, as a chip to break the ice.
choices.risk_hint: The origin of the gift may arouse suspicion

text.content: Chen Ji retrieved an ancient jade slip from his spatial artifact—it was something he had chanced upon in an ancient ruin, its contents on formation essentials coincidentally sharing similar principles with the chess path the princess excelled in. This gift was neither too light nor too heavy, just perfect.

The imperial garden, Phoenix Pavilion. Princess Taiping lounged on a beauty's couch in her goose-yellow palace attire, a white jade chess piece pinched between her fingers, seemingly lost in thought. The maid reported: 'Your Highness, Master Longyuan has arrived.' She raised her eyes, a spark of interest flickering within: 'Admit him.'

Chen Ji walked slowly into the garden, his gaze straight ahead. He performed a standard ministerial bow toward the princess—neither excessively humble nor deliberately aloof. Princess Taiping studied him, then suddenly laughed lightly: 'Master Longyuan is indeed a handsome man. I heard you made that troublemaker Han Lie eat humble pie last night?'

dialogue.content: Your Highness flatters me. I merely spoke the truth, which is hardly an accomplishment.

text.content: Princess Taiping's smile deepened. She gestured for Chen Ji to sit, personally pouring him a cup of tea. 'Speaking the truth?' She pushed the teacup toward him. 'Who in the imperial capital doesn't know what kind of person Han Lie is? Even I must give him three points of face. For someone newly arrived to make him touch a tiger's whiskers, you either have something to rely on, or...' she paused, 'you simply don't know how to write the character for death.'

Chen Ji took the teacup but did not drink. He calmly said: 'Your Highness speaks truly. I am indeed new here and do not understand the capital's customs.' He raised his eyes, his gaze calmly meeting the princess's. 'But I believe some things are not about understanding customs, but whether they are worth the risk.'

A gleam flashed in Princess Taiping's eyes. She suddenly sat up straight, looking at Chen Ji with great interest: 'Oh? Does Master think allying with the Crown Prince is worth the risk?' Chen Ji shook his head: 'What is worth risking is never the Crown Prince, but—' he smiled faintly, 'Your Highness.'

At these words, the entire garden fell silent. Princess Taiping's smile froze on her face, her gaze suddenly turning sharp. The maids behind her simultaneously placed their hands on their sword hilts, ready to take lives at the slightest provocation. Yet Chen Ji sat steadily as before, as if oblivious to that chilling killing intent.

dialogue.content: Your Highness need not be nervous. I did not come today to threaten you, but to... cooperate.

text.content: Princess Taiping suddenly burst out laughing, laughing so hard she doubled over. The maids exchanged bewildered glances, not understanding why their mistress was so amused. When she finally stopped laughing and wiped the tears from her eyes, she pointed at Chen Ji and said: 'Interesting. In my twenty-three years, this is the first time I've encountered a strategist who dares say 'cooperate' before me.' She sobered her expression. 'Speak then, how do you wish to cooperate?'

Chen Ji took the ancient jade slip from his sleeve and presented it with both hands: 'This is a gift for Your Highness.' Princess Taiping took the jade slip, her divine sense probing within, and her expression slightly changed. She examined it front and back for a long while, then suddenly looked up, her gaze burning as she stared at Chen Ji: 'Where did you obtain this?'

dialogue.content: A fortunate encounter. If Your Highness likes it, please consider it a small token from me. As for cooperation... Your Highness already has calculations in mind, so why ask me?

text.content: Princess Taiping stared at him for a long while, then suddenly stood up and walked behind him, gazing down at his profile from above. Chen Ji remained motionless, letting her examine him freely. After a long silence, the princess softly said: 'You are very confident.' Chen Ji smiled faintly: 'Not confident, but... with no other choice.'

Princess Taiping returned to her seat, lounging on the couch once more. This time, her gaze at Chen Ji was no longer playful, but carried a hint of seriousness. 'Very well, I shall remember you.' She lifted her teacup. 'Master Longyuan, my imperial garden is always open to you. However—' she paused, 'I despise being schemed against. If you dare play any tricks...'

dialogue.content: Your Highness can rest easy. I never scheme against friends, only against enemies. And Your Highness... is暂时不是敌人.

text.content: Princess Taiping raised an eyebrow: "For now?" Chen Ji rose to take his leave. Before leaving, he turned back to glance at her. That gaze carried an indescribable meaning: "Your Highness, who can say what the future holds?" With that, he cupped his fists in farewell, leaving the princess alone, lost in thought as she gazed at his departing figure.

Leaving the Imperial Garden, Chen Ji walked without stopping. He knew that the words he had just spoken had sparked Princess Taiping's interest in him—this was both good and bad. The good part was that he had established a connection with the princess; the bad part was that the princess was no easy opponent. Once her curiosity turned into suspicion, it would bring deadly disaster.

He raised his eyes to look at the sky above the imperial palace, where dragon qi coiled, faintly exuding a chilling pressure that made one's heart tremble. This city hid too many secrets, and too many dangers. His entry into it under the name "Master Longyuan" was merely the first step. How many hidden reefs and lethal traps lay ahead, he did not know. But one thing he was certain of—Chen Nian was waiting for him.

Returning to the inn, Chen Ji dismissed his attendants and sat alone by the window. He took from his chest a yellowed page bearing fragments of prophecy from the Tianji Record. "The Eye of Heavenly Dao..." he murmured to himself. "What is it you truly want?" Outside the window, the night wind rose, stirring the loose hair at his temples. His gaze was as deep as an abyss, seemingly hiding endless schemes and resolve.

This day, the name "Master Longyuan" officially spread throughout the imperial court. Some said he was resourceful and full of strategies, others said he was recklessly daring, and still others claimed he had the backing of an unequaled master behind him. And at this moment, Chen Ji was facing a solitary lamp, writing down all the gains and losses of this night. Han Lie's grudge, the Crown Prince's dependence, the Princess's curiosity—three threads had all been set in motion.

He set down his brush and gazed at the night sky beyond the window. Chen Nian's words still echoed in his ears. "Don't trust anyone, including yourself." He suddenly let out a light laugh, that smile carrying bitterness, self-mockery, and a resolute determination to break all bridges. Very well, then he would trust no one. He trusted only his own chess game, his own schemes, and his own—fate.
